name: Robotics, Automation and Physical AI
thesis: Physical AI is moving from demos to early production: Tesla is pouring a record $25 billion plus into 2026 capex across AI, Optimus and robotaxi, Hyundai plans a 30,000 per year Atlas factory, and Waymo is doubling paid rides. Humanoid volumes are still tiny (about 18,000 units globally in 2025 per IDC), so the reliable money today is in the parts every robot needs: precision reducers, bearings, frameless motors, rare earth magnets, vision sensors and AI compute. China already leads humanoid shipments and controls most rare earth magnet supply, which makes magnets and reducers the true chokepoints. Expect most humanoid makers to disappoint on timelines while component suppliers, compute and warehouse automation earn real revenue.
money_source: Tesla raised 2026 capex guidance to more than $25 billion (vs $8.5 billion spent in 2025), for AI training, chips, Optimus manufacturing capacity and robotaxi, and expects negative free cash flow for the rest of 2026. Figure AI raised over $1 billion at a $39 billion valuation (Sept 2025); humanoid startups raised $3.2 billion globally in 2025. Hyundai plans a factory for 30,000 Atlas robots per year by 2028. Waymo (Alphabet) is funding a push from about 500,000 to 1 million paid rides per week by end of 2026. The US Department of Defense took an equity stake in MP Materials with a 10 year $110 per kg NdPr price floor (July 2025). Symbotic holds a $22.5 billion backlog, mostly Walmart.

facts: 2026 capex guidance raised to more than $25 billion, up from $20 billion in January and about $8.5 billion spent in 2025; CFO expects negative free cash flow for the rest of 2026.
Q2 2026 revenue $28.24 billion; adjusted EPS $0.33 vs about $0.50 expected; shares fell about 11% after hours on July 22, 2026.

First generation Optimus production lines being installed at Fremont, limited production from late July or August 2026, high volume pushed to 2027; Musk called it the hardest product Tesla has ever scaled, with about 10,000 unique parts.
Musk said in April 2025 that China's rare earth magnet export licensing affected Optimus arm actuators.
Tesla robotaxi still operated only in Austin as of mid 2026 with limited fully driverless vehicles, while Waymo ran in 10 plus US metros.

pipeline.product: Tesla Optimus first generation production at Fremont
pipeline.timing: Limited production from Q3 2026; high volume 2027 (reported targets of 1,000 per week then 2,000 to 2,500 per week are industry reports via Morgan Stanley, unverified by Tesla)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Each humanoid needs 20 to 40 harmonic reducers and 25 to 30 actuators; a real ramp would be the largest new order source for reducers, roller screws, frameless motors and NdFeB magnets.

pipeline.product: Hyundai and Boston Dynamics Atlas factory
pipeline.timing: Atlas deployed at Hyundai Metaplant Georgia for parts sequencing from 2028; 30,000 units per year capacity targeted by 2028
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: A second large Western humanoid buyer of actuators and sensors, plus Hyundai Mobis style in house parts.

pipeline.product: Waymo expansion to Denver, San Diego, Tampa, Las Vegas and international cities
pipeline.timing: Through end of 2026; target 1 million paid rides per week
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: More vehicles means more lidar, cameras, compute and fleet maintenance demand; validates robotaxi unit economics.

pipeline.product: Nvidia Jetson Thor and new mainstream Jetson Thor modules (July 2026), Toyota physical AI collaboration
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Nvidia becomes the default robot brain, making compute a toll on every humanoid and AMR platform.

pipeline.product: MP Materials heavy rare earth separation at Mountain Pass and 10X magnet campus in Northlake, Texas
pipeline.timing: Heavy RE separation commissioning later in 2026; 10X commissioning 2028
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: First scaled non-China magnet source for US robot and EV motor makers.

pipeline.product: Unitree IPO in China (plans to raise 6.1 billion yuan, about $9 billion valuation reported)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Gives Chinese humanoid supply chain a public valuation benchmark; more capital to Chinese reducer and motor suppliers.

pipeline.product: Section 232 investigation into robotics and industrial machinery (opened September 2025)
pipeline.timing: Outcome pending as of sources reviewed
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Tariffs on imported robots and machinery would hit Japanese, European and Chinese robot makers and favor US assembly.

layers.name: Humanoid robot makers (OEMs)
layers.why: They set the demand signal for the entire parts chain, but volumes are tiny and timelines keep slipping.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Many entrants (Tesla, Figure, Boston Dynamics, Unitree, AgiBot, UBTech, Xpeng) with heavy funding; no one controls supply, and Chinese makers already lead shipments (Unitree over 5,500 in 2025; Unitree, AgiBot and UBTech over 60% of global shipments).

companies.name: Tesla
companies.role: Optimus humanoid, FSD and robotaxi, in house AI chips
companies.note: Valuation rests heavily on Optimus and robotaxi; capex now about 3x 2025 and FCF negative near term.

companies.name: Hyundai Motor
companies.role: Owner of Boston Dynamics (Atlas), anchor customer for its own robots
companies.note: OTC listing is illiquid GDR.

companies.name: UBTech Robotics
companies.role: Walker S industrial humanoids
companies.note: Hong Kong listed; heavily loss making.

companies.name: XPeng
companies.role: EV maker developing IRON humanoid and robotaxi
companies.note: Robotics is optional upside on an EV business.

companies.name: Figure AI
companies.role: General purpose humanoid, BMW deployment
companies.note: $39B post money valuation (Sept 2025); plans 100,000 humanoids over four years. Not investable publicly.

companies.name: Unitree Robotics
companies.role: Largest humanoid shipper by volume
companies.note: Over 5,500 humanoids shipped in 2025.

layers.name: Precision reducers, actuators and bearings
layers.why: Every joint needs a reducer, motor, bearing and encoder; a humanoid has 25 to 30 actuators and 20 to 40 harmonic reducers, so parts content per robot is large regardless of which OEM wins.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Strain wave (harmonic) gearing and planetary roller screws need precision metallurgy and years of qualification; a handful of Japanese, German and Chinese firms supply most volume.

companies.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
companies.role: Strain wave gears, the reference reducer for robot joints
companies.note: Booked about 1.3B yen of humanoid orders in one quarter and guided about 2.5B yen for FY3/26, possibly double or triple in FY3/27. Tokyo listing only.

companies.name: Leaderdrive (Suzhou Lvdi)
companies.role: Chinese harmonic reducer leader
companies.note: 2025 revenue 570M yuan, +47%. Not accessible to most US accounts.

companies.name: Nabtesco
companies.role: RV (cycloidal) reducers for industrial robots
companies.note: Dominant in heavy industrial robot joints.

companies.name: THK
companies.role: Linear guides, ball screws

companies.name: Schaeffler
companies.role: Bearings and integrated humanoid actuators
companies.note: May 2026: preferred supplier for over 50% of UK company Humanoid's joint actuators through 2031.

companies.name: Timken
companies.role: Precision bearings and gear drives

companies.name: RBC Bearings
companies.role: Precision bearings, mostly aerospace and industrial
companies.note: Robotics exposure small; quality compounder.

companies.name: Nidec
companies.role: Precision motors and actuators

companies.name: Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls
companies.role: Thermal parts; widely reported as Optimus actuator supplier
companies.note: Optimus supplier role is reported in media, unverified this session.

layers.name: Rare earth magnets and materials
layers.why: Compact high torque motors in robot joints and EVs need NdFeB magnets; China controls most refining and magnet making and imposed export licensing on heavy rare earths and related magnets in April 2025.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Single country concentration; Musk said licensing hit Optimus. Non-China supply (MP, Lynas) is only now scaling with government support.

companies.name: MP Materials
companies.role: US rare earth mine, separation and magnet maker
companies.note: DoD equity partner and $110 per kg NdPr price floor for 10 years; Apple recycled magnet supply deal; 10X Texas magnet plant commissioning 2028. Stock already rerated sharply on government backing.

companies.name: Lynas Rare Earths
companies.role: Largest non-China separated rare earths producer

layers.name: Robot brains: AI compute and vision chips
layers.why: Training in simulation and running inference on board both require GPUs and SoCs; this is where most physical AI dollars land today.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Nvidia's Jetson Thor and Isaac and Omniverse stack are the de facto standard; image sensors are dominated by Sony.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.role: Jetson Thor robot computer, DRIVE AV platform, Isaac and Cosmos simulation
companies.note: Automotive and robotics revenue was $586M in Q2 FY2026, +69%; from FY2027 it is folded into a new Edge Computing segment, reducing transparency.

companies.name: Ambarella
companies.role: Edge AI vision SoCs for cameras, robots and vehicles
companies.note: Small cap, high multiple.

companies.name: Sony Group
companies.role: CMOS image sensors used in robot and vehicle cameras

companies.name: Analog Devices
companies.role: Motor control, encoders, sensing and power for robots

layers.name: Perception: lidar and machine vision
layers.why: Robotaxis, AMRs and humanoids need 3D perception; lidar costs have fallen enough for mass production in Chinese cars.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Hesai has scale (1.62M units in 2025) and cost leadership, but Tesla's camera only approach caps the market and US policy restricts Chinese lidar.

companies.name: Hesai Group
companies.role: Lidar leader for ADAS and robotics
companies.note: 2025 shipments 1,620,406 (+223%), revenue RMB 3.03B (+45.8%), first full year profit; 2026 shipment outlook 3 to 3.5M units. US national security listing and Pentagon list risk.

companies.name: Ouster
companies.role: Digital lidar for industrial, robotics, smart infrastructure
companies.note: Guided Q3 2026 revenue $54.5M to $57.5M; still loss making.

companies.name: Cognex
companies.role: Machine vision for factory and logistics automation

layers.name: Batteries and power for mobile robots
layers.why: Humanoids and AMRs need dense, swappable packs; Atlas uses a self swappable battery.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Cell supply is abundant but concentrated in China; robot packs are small volumes versus EVs.

companies.name: CATL
companies.role: World's largest battery cell maker
companies.note: Robot demand is immaterial to CATL today.

layers.name: Industrial automation and robot arms
layers.why: Reshoring, labor shortages and data center and semiconductor fab construction are lifting factory automation orders now, independent of humanoids.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Mature oligopoly in robot arms and PLCs with strong installed bases; Chinese makers are gaining share at home.

companies.name: Rockwell Automation
companies.role: PLCs, drives, motion, software
companies.note: Fiscal 2026 orders growing double digits per management, citing warehouse automation, data centers, semis, energy.

companies.name: Fanuc
companies.role: Largest industrial robot and CNC maker

companies.name: Yaskawa Electric
companies.role: Robots, servo motors, drives

companies.name: ABB
companies.role: Automation and electrification; robotics unit sale to SoftBank reported in 2025
companies.note: Robotics divestiture status unverified this session.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.role: Universal Robots collaborative arms, MiR AMRs, chip test
companies.note: Robotics is a minority of revenue; semi test drives the stock.

companies.name: Siemens
companies.role: Factory automation, PLCs, industrial software

layers.name: Warehouse and logistics automation
layers.why: Retailers are spending to automate distribution centers now, with contracted backlogs; this is the most proven robot revenue stream.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Symbotic is tied to Walmart; Amazon builds in house; integration know how is the barrier.

companies.name: Symbotic
companies.role: AI driven warehouse automation systems
companies.note: Backlog about $22.5B; about 13% converts in next 12 months. Walmart option for 400 back of store systems not in backlog. Heavy customer concentration and past accounting restatement.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.role: Operates over 1 million robots; Amazon Robotics in house
companies.note: About 75% of global deliveries are robot assisted.

companies.name: Zebra Technologies
companies.role: Scanners, RFID, warehouse AMRs

layers.name: Autonomous vehicles and robotaxis
layers.why: Robotaxis are the first physical AI product with recurring consumer revenue at scale; Waymo has proven driverless operations across many metros.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Regulatory approval city by city and safety record are the gates; Waymo has a large lead in driverless miles.

companies.name: Alphabet (Waymo)
companies.role: Waymo driverless robotaxi
companies.note: About 500,000 paid rides per week early 2026, target 1 million by year end; 10 plus US markets.

companies.name: Uber Technologies
companies.role: Demand aggregator partnering with AV makers
companies.note: Benefits if AVs plug into its network; hurt if Waymo and Tesla go direct.

companies.name: Mobileye Global
companies.role: ADAS chips and AV systems
companies.note: 2026 revenue guide $1.97B to $2.02B (+4% to 7%); $250M buyback.

companies.name: Pony.ai
companies.role: Chinese robotaxi operator
companies.note: Fleet and financial figures unverified this session; loss making.

companies.name: WeRide
companies.role: Chinese robotaxi and robobus operator
companies.note: Unverified figures; loss making.

companies.name: Aurora Innovation
companies.role: Driverless trucking in Texas
companies.note: Pre revenue scale; dilution risk. Figures unverified this session.

second_order.idea: Sell the shovels, not the humanoid
second_order.why: Component and compute suppliers get paid on prototypes and pilots even if humanoid timelines slip; Harmonic Drive's humanoid orders doubling or tripling is the tell.

second_order.idea: Rare earth independence as a policy trade
second_order.why: Government price floors and equity stakes reduce downside; exposure covers EVs, defense and robots simultaneously.

second_order.idea: Data center construction is lifting industrial automation now
second_order.why: Rockwell cites data centers and semis as order drivers; less speculative than humanoids.

second_order.idea: Robotaxi scale helps fleet services, insurance data and mapping more than car makers
second_order.why: Waymo doubling rides means the platform owner and the demand network capture the economics.

second_order.idea: Options angle: high implied volatility in speculative robot names
second_order.why: Elevated IV on timeline headlines rewards covered calls on held shares; avoid naked puts on loss making names (OUST, AUR, PONY) where dilution can gap the stock. Framework, not advice.
